outcome: Give logistics coo / supply chain director a governed method to improve customs rejection rate using commercial invoices, HS codes and shipment manifests, with final decisions retained by named staff.
overview: Cross-Border Customs Document Validation addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses commercial invoices, HS codes and shipment manifests. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is customs rejection rate, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: commercial invoices, HS codes and shipment manifests; define customs rejection rate and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for customs rejection rate
